R4-1.headline: Likely: if the US weakens, its money role passes to a crowd (gold, the euro, smaller currencies), not to China. The yuan reaches 10% of reserves only about 9 to 18 years after an opening that has not happened.
up: COFER shows the dollar falling while gold and 'other' currencies, not the yuan, take the share (next print late December 2026)
China keeps its $50,000 personal quota and guided fixing through 2027
Euro credit to non-residents keeps growing faster than dollar credit in the next BIS release
down: China lifts the personal quota and lets the yuan float, and the yuan share rises more than 1 point a year
The yuan passes 5% of SWIFT payments for three months in a row
A US promise failure (Fed capture or a tax or freeze on foreign Treasury holdings) sends reserves to one rival instead of many
R4-1.watch: IMF COFER Q3 2026 in late December 2026: dollar below 56%, yuan above 2.5% or euro above 22%

R4-3.headline: Likely: the EU slides slowly against the US but does not fall. The real tail is a France- or Italy-led euro crisis (20% by 2028), not exit or impoverishment.
up: France passes a 2027 budget and the OAT-Bund spread falls back below 150bp
The April 2027 IMF WEO keeps the EU's purchasing-power income near 72% of the US
Euro support stays above 80% in the next Eurobarometer
down: The OAT-Bund spread closes above 250bp for ten sessions without ECB action
A National Rally president elected in May 2027 opens a budget clash with Brussels
German chemicals output falls below 75 (2021 = 100) and euro-area GDP contracts with inflation above 3%
R4-3.watch: The French budget vote on 2026-10-27 and the OAT-Bund spread against 200bp

R4-4.headline: Likely: breaking away does not improve a country's chances. Brexit cost the UK about 6% to 8% of GDP per head, and the winning model is in the single market with its own currency, not outside the EU.
up: New Brexit studies (OBR, NIESR, Bank of England) keep the long-run cost at 4% or more
Switzerland ratifies the Bilaterals III package with the EU, showing outsiders move closer, not further
Poland and Sweden keep outgrowing the euro area without leaving the single market
down: UK growth beats the euro area by more than 1 point a year for three years
A country outside the euro and the single market converges faster than Poland
A peer-reviewed study finds the Brexit cost below 3%
R4-4.watch: The Swiss National Council vote and likely referendum on Bilaterals III in 2027

R4-7.headline: Likely: Europe's money goes West, about 55% of net outbound capital to North America in 2028 to 2035, while factories split between the US, Asia and Europe's periphery and Latin America stays near 6%.
up: TIC data keep showing rising euro-area holdings of US equities and Treasuries
UNCTAD's 2027 report shows European greenfield projects concentrated in the US
Henley's 2027 report keeps Latin America out of the top ten millionaire destinations
down: Euro-area holdings of US equities fall below $5T for six months without a price fall to explain it
Supply-chain manufacturing FDI into Southeast Asia rebounds above $31B with Europe as a top source
EU-Mercosur enters into force and Mexico's greenfield announcements return above $40B
R4-7.watch: The monthly TIC release in mid-November 2026 (September data): euro-area holdings of US securities

R4-8.headline: More likely than not: the owner's regional cautions hold on average but are too broad. The UAE, Morocco, Rwanda, Botswana and Kazakhstan clear bars that Mexico and Brazil do not.
up: ACLED's December 2026 index keeps Mexico and Brazil in the ten most violent countries
WJP 2026 or 2027 keeps the UAE above every Latin American country except Uruguay, Costa Rica and Chile
The UAE returns to the top of millionaire inflows once Gulf security normalises
down: The Gulf war widens and the UAE suffers a lasting outflow of foreign residents
Mexico and Brazil improve sharply on rule of law and violence
Morocco or Kenya enter ACLED's major conflict list
R4-8.watch: ACLED Conflict Index in December 2026: whether the Gulf enters it and whether Mexico and Brazil stay in the top ten

R4-9.headline: Likely: markets price a French problem and a slow European discount, not a collapse or a US downfall. No market above $1M traded is more than 15 points from the desk.
up: Italy's spread stays below 150bp while France's widens
The Bund keeps rising with French yields instead of falling as a haven
Exit markets stay thin and below 10%
down: A deep market (above $1M) on euro exit or a French default appears and prices above 15%
The Bund yield falls below 3% while the French spread passes 200bp, a redenomination pattern
The Le Pen price moves above 61 or below 31 with no change in desk odds
R4-9.watch: The ECB meeting on 2026-10-29 (hold priced 97.85) and any reference to TPI

R4-10.headline: Likely: France is the euro area's weak link for now, with its spread near 172bp and above Italy, but the stress stays French unless Italy's spread passes 150bp.
up: Moody's cuts France to A1 and the 2027 budget fails or passes only by Article 49.3
The OAT-Bund spread closes above 200bp for five sessions
The National Rally candidate stays above 45% in the 2027 market
down: A credible 2027 budget passes and the spread falls below 120bp
Italy's spread passes France's again, moving the weak link back to Italy
The ECB signals TPI eligibility for France
R4-10.watch: Moody's France decision, due 2026-10-23 after the close and not yet published at the time of writing

R4-11.headline: Likely: Poland's catch-up is real and continues, but its deficit (7.2% of GDP, the EU's largest) makes it a fiscal risk, not a safe haven.
up: The 2027 deficit stays above 6% while the 10-year yield stays above 6%
Fitch or another agency cuts Poland's rating
Growth stays above 3% while public spending stays near 50% of GDP
down: A post-election budget cuts the deficit below 4% with defence protected
The 10-year yield falls back below 5.5%
Poland's growth falls to the EU average
R4-11.watch: Poland's October 2027 parliamentary election and the 10-year yield against 6%
